input.question: IPv6, the new and improved internet protocol?
input.ground_truth: The main advantage of IPv6 as I understand it is the addition of an extremely large number of IP addresses. Basically an IP address is like the address to your house or a phone number; it is a unique number that allows other computers to send letters (or packets of info) to your computer and you can send letters back to them. When IPv4 was developed they never imagined they would use up all of the IP addresses but now since everyone has so many devices connected to the Internet we are reaching the limit so they created IPv6. The same thing can happen with phone numbers, almost everyone has a cell phone now so eventually we will run out of phone numbers. IPv6 is essentially like adding another sub-area code to a phone number or like another sub-zip code to an address to accommodate the ever expanding human population. (This is a gross over simplification but hey, you are five so what do you know?)

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: IPv6, the new and improved internet protocol?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how I’d explain it to a 5-year-old:

Imagine the internet is like a big city, and every house in the city needs an address so people can find it. The old addresses (IPv4) are starting to run out, like if you only had 10 numbers to give to everyone in a big town.

So, we made new, bigger addresses (IPv6). These new addresses are like having more numbers and letters to use, so everyone in the whole world can have their own special address. This makes it easier and better for the internet to grow and for everyone to find each other’s houses!
